supply_shock_playbook.conclusion: On a random non-event date the same statistics are +5.4% (peak) and +0.7% (settle): a 20-session maximum is positive on 87% of ordinary dates, so a group's median peak only means something relative to that. Announced or physical supply removal >0.5 mbpd (n=21): median peak +12.1%, settle +4.3% (p = 0.0005 / 0.0445 vs placebo; 0.0015 / 0.1027 year-matched): it differs from an ordinary date on peak (above). Geopolitical threat, no supply removed (n=10): median peak +4.0%, settle +0.5% (p = 0.4897 / 0.9443 vs placebo; 0.6419 / 0.9564 year-matched): it is indistinguishable from an ordinary date. Supply removal vs threat-only directly: p = 0.0309 (peak), 0.3874 (settle). Above the unmatched placebo at 5% but not the year-matched one: Announced OPEC(+) production cut (n=7, peak p = 0.0264 vs 0.0898 year-matched). Above the year-matched placebo at 5% but not the unmatched one: Armed conflict (n=15, peak p = 0.2016 vs 0.0428 year-matched), All defined events (n=35, peak p = 0.0916 vs 0.0303 year-matched). Caveats: event dates and groupings were chosen with hindsight; the groups overlap; some events are close enough that their windows share sessions (hurricane_katrina_2005 and hurricane_rita_2005, 19 sessions apart; saudi_russia_price_war_2020 and opec_record_cut_2020, 24 sessions apart; opec_cut_2023 and iran_tanker_seizure_2023, 22 sessions apart; lebanon_hezbollah_2024 and iran_israel_oct_2024, 6 sessions apart), so members of a group are not all independent; and these p-values are not adjusted for the number of groups tested (see data/research_ledger.json).

supply_lost.definition: supply_mbpd > 0.5: physical outages (wars, attacks, hurricane shut-ins), sanctioned export losses and announced OPEC(+) quota cuts
supply_lost.label: Announced or physical supply removal >0.5 mbpd

threat_only.definition: supply_mbpd == 0, excluding bearish supply gluts and demand events: conflict, strait and escalation scares
threat_only.label: Geopolitical threat, no supply removed

placebo.exclusion: sessions within 19 of an event (its base, window or settle would touch the event) are excluded

priced_in_stats.definition: day-0 move vs the previous close; further rise = highest close over the next 19 trading days vs the day-0 close (day 0 itself excluded)

returns.series: CL=F with roll days rebuilt as same-contract returns (EIA contract 1 and 2)

variance_risk_premium.method: OVX (the CBOE Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index, a 30-calendar-day implied vol from options on the USO ETF, not on CL futures, so it carries a basis to front-month WTI) vs realized vol over the next 20 trading days (about 29 calendar days), non-overlapping. Short-vol proxies: vol swap = IV - RV; variance swap per unit vega = (IV^2 - RV^2) / (2 IV). Timing: short-variance P&L regressed on OVX minus the model's forecast (Newey-West t), and rich = that spread above its trailing median.

sharpe_positive_test.method: one-sided test of Sharpe > 0 on the non-overlapping periods, standard error of Mertens (2002) / Opdyke (2007) for i.i.d. non-normal returns: sqrt((1 - skewness * SR + (raw kurtosis - 1) / 4 * SR^2) / n), SR per period; raw kurtosis = excess_kurtosis + 3

variance_risk_premium.vol_points_caveat: With zero variance premium (IV^2 = E[RV^2]) a 20-session realized vol still falls below implied vol in most periods and E[IV - RV] > 0 (Jensen's inequality), so comparing the share of positive periods with 50%, or the mean premium in vol points with 0, overstates the evidence for a premium; zero_premium_null gives both as expected with no premium. The short vol-swap proxy's mean has the same bias, so its Sharpe test against 0 overstates the evidence too.

zero_premium_null.method: zero premium: the per-period ratios RV^2 / IV^2 rescaled to mean 1 (their observed shape kept); share_positive_pct and mean_premium_vol_pts are the share of periods with IV > RV and the mean IV - RV expected with no premium. Test of the observed share against it: stationary block bootstrap of the rescaled ratios, re-estimating the null share in every draw; one-sided.

vol_target_overlay.method: Weekly rebalanced long front-month WTI, rolled at each expiry (same-contract returns); position = min(cap, target vol / forecast vol), sized on the variance-consistent forecast. Trailing-vol sizing uses 22-day realized vol; costs on every unit of turnover. Sharpe differences use a stationary block bootstrap.

interval_80.method: adaptive conformal inference on out-of-sample log errors (Gibbs-Candes 2021)

live_record.promotion_rule: The promotion test is pinned to one pair: HAR-IV v2 (model version har-iv/2), the model of record, against the HAR-IV-range challenger (key har_iv_range). The challenger replaces the model of record if, on the first 52 independent resolved weeks where both were forecast, its mean QLIKE is lower with a one-sided Diebold-Mariano p below 0.10 (Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold, Student t with 51 degrees of freedom). The test is run once, on that fixed sample. Forecasts from another model version or challenger are recorded but never enter it; a different challenger would start a new, separately declared test. A maintainer applies the verdict.
live_record.note: Each forecast is scored on the realized volatility of the five settlement-to-settlement returns after the first CL settlement (14:30 ET) at least an hour after it was issued and recorded, one session or more later than the backtest's window. The record is sealed just before each git commit; an entry not sealed more than five minutes before that settlement is marked late_commit and never scored, so every scored forecast was committed before any price it is scored on.
live_record.direction_note: Direction accuracy is not evidence of skill: on simulated returns with nothing to forecast, the backtest's noise floor is 75.2%, because a five-session realized vol is a noisy estimate that reverts toward its mean. QLIKE is the skill measure.
